transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, so… I guess what finally got me to come in is I can’t keep my head on one thing anymore. Like at work, I’ll be trying to finish an estimate or one of those code forms, and then a tool goes off, or my phone buzzes, or I suddenly think of some new setup for the workshop—actually I’ve been meaning to reorganize the whole back wall because it’s a mess—and then I’m completely off track.

Then I come back and I’ve mixed up parts of different jobs, or I don’t remember where I left off. It’s getting frustrating, and it’s starting to cause problems.
When did you first start having trouble focusing or staying on task like this? Was it something you noticed even as a kid, or is it more recent?

No, not really as a kid. I mean, I could get distracted sometimes, but this kind of thing… it’s more recent. It’s been building for maybe seven months now, around when we took on the mortgage for the workshop and all the equipment. That’s when it started feeling like my attention was slipping more and more.

The mortgage thing is a whole story too, because the bank made it sound simple at first, and then suddenly there were forms and inspections and—anyway, yeah, about seven months.
Have you noticed yourself feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy, like your workshop or other hobbies?

Um… I’m not sure. I wouldn’t say I’ve been hopeless, exactly. I mean, I get frustrated, yeah, but that’s different, right?

With the workshop, I still care about it. It’s just—there’s always some little thing pulling at me, like the outlets on the west wall still aren’t where I want them, and I keep thinking if I just redo that whole corner it’ll make everything run smoother. But as far as feeling down or not enjoying anything… I don’t think that’s really been the main issue.
Have you found yourself feeling restless, fidgety, or unusually on edge lately, like you can't sit still or your mind is constantly racing?

Yeah… restless is probably the right word. I feel like if I sit down too long, I’m just wasting time. I’ll be bouncing from job sites to putting together bids, then I’m back in the workshop rewiring test panels or messing with some home-automation idea.

And the problem is I’ll start one thing before the last thing is actually done. Like I’ve got this lighting-control setup half-finished, and then I’ll suddenly think, no, the garage door sensors should tie into it too, and then I’m pulling parts for that instead. It’s like my mind is already three steps ahead and my hands are trying to catch up.
Have you ever had periods where you felt unusually energized, needed less sleep, or felt like your thoughts were racing so much that you couldn’t slow them down?

Yeah, the sleep part, definitely. For months now I’ve been getting maybe three, four hours, and then I’m just… up. Like before dawn, wide awake, ready to start pricing materials or answering emails.

Sometimes I’ll sketch out another system layout, like for the workshop or some wiring idea, and it doesn’t feel like I barely slept. It feels like I got a full night, which is weird, because normally I’d think that would catch up with me. The supplier opens early anyway, and if I can get ahead on pricing copper or breakers before calls start coming in—sorry, I’m wandering. But yeah, I haven’t needed much sleep lately.

Have there been times when you felt so confident or powerful that you thought you could take on more than usual, or when you got involved in multiple projects or activities that others might consider risky or overly ambitious?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t think of it as “powerful,” exactly, but I have been looking at bigger jobs and thinking, why not me? Like commercial jobs, not just the smaller residential stuff.

And I’ve had this idea that I could bring on a crew and train them up myself right now. I know, technically, there’s licensing stuff and experience gaps I’d have to sort out, and part of me does know I’m not totally there for every kind of job. But then I start thinking, well, I can learn it fast, I can organize it better than half the guys doing it anyway, and if I just get the right people—actually, my cousin knows a guy who did warehouse lighting and he was terrible at paperwork, so it’s not like everyone out there is so buttoned up.

So… yeah, I guess I’ve been taking on—or trying to take on—more than maybe I’m really set up for.

Have there been times when your mood was noticeably more irritable, or when you felt unusually confident, excited, or driven in a way that was different from your usual self—even if others around you didn’t see it that way?

Yeah, I guess that has happened. I’ll get in this really pumped-up mood, like I’m talking about our little shop like we’re about to become the main solar outfit in town, you know? Like it all feels obvious to me—get the vans, line up the installs, train a couple guys, and we’re off.

But then if my wife says, “Have you actually priced that out?” or one of the apprentices asks if the plan makes sense, I can get… sharp. Like way sharper than I need to be. I’ll snap back over nothing, like they’re trying to slow me down or don’t see what I see. Then later I’m thinking, why did I come at them like that? So yeah, excited and driven, but irritable too, I guess.
